        Voice

        ★ = higher quality. On iPhone you can add more natural voices: Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices → English, then download an "Enhanced" or "Premium" voice (Karen and Lee are Australian). Reload the app afterwards.

        About the data
        Approved mobile camera sites, not confirmed cameras. Solid pins mark the listed street within its suburb; faded dashed pins are rough spots (usually long highways) placed at the suburb. Numbered circles group nearby sites; the ring colour shows the highest hotspot level inside. Hotspot ratings (High/Medium/Standard) come from Victoria's reason codes; other states publish no rating. Square icons are fixed cameras: speed, red light, average speed (dashed line joins a section) and phone/seatbelt, from each state's published list (NSW, SA and ACT positions are official GPS; others are placed on the listed road). Lists: State of Victoria (Oct 2026), Transport for NSW (Sep 2026), Queensland Police Service, SA Police and Access Canberra, under their open licences. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

        Alerts on this route
          Simulation only. You're only warned about cameras on the road you're driving along. A mobile zone covers the chosen length either side of its listed spot. Warnings come about 25 seconds ahead at your speed (300 m at 40 km/h, 420 m at 60, 760 m at 110, never more than 1 km). Cameras that only check the other direction stay quiet. Inside an average-speed section you see your running average. Once an alert starts it stays until you've passed it, then a soft two-note tone says the zone has ended. Routes by OSRM (OpenStreetMap data).
